passages.title: A Wrong Turn on the Mountain Road
passages.text:
Last summer, Hung borrowed his uncle's car for a weekend trip. On the main road out of the city, a large sign showed the **speed limit**: sixty kilometres an hour. Hung stayed below it, even when a line of impatient drivers formed behind him. Later, the road began to climb into the hills, and a new sign appeared: **no overtaking**. This was important, because the bends were sharp and he could not see far ahead.

A young driver in a small red car ignored the sign. He tried to **overtake** Hung on a bend, just as a bus came round the corner from the opposite direction. Luckily, both cars stopped in time, but everyone was shaken. Hung, whose phone battery had died, then followed the wrong road and **ended up** in a tiny village he had never heard of. An old man at a café drew him a map on a paper napkin. "Better to arrive late than not to arrive at all," he said. Hung agreed and drove home slowly.
passages.summary_vi: Hùng lái xe của chú đi chơi cuối tuần, gặp biển giới hạn tốc độ và cấm vượt, suýt tai nạn vì một tài xế trẻ vượt xe, rồi lạc vào một ngôi làng lạ và được một cụ già vẽ đường về.

passages.title: Learning to Cook
passages.text:
Mai had never been **a good cook**, and her friends often joked about it. When she moved into her own flat, she decided to change that. Her first rule was simple: **follow a recipe** carefully and never guess the measurements. Her second rule was to check that she **had all the ingredients** before she started, because last month she discovered halfway through making soup that there was no salt in the house.

On Sunday she made a big meal from a cookbook her grandmother gave her. First she had to **boil** the potatoes in a saucepan for fifteen minutes. While they cooked, she **fried** some onions in a frying pan and **grilled** two pieces of fish under the grill until the skin was crisp. Then she **roasted** a chicken in the oven until it turned golden. For dessert she **baked** an apple cake, which smelled wonderful when it came out. Roasting and baking both use the oven, but roasting is for meat or vegetables with oil, while baking is for cakes and bread. Her friends tasted everything and admitted that it was delicious. Mai smiled: she was finally getting better.

passages.title: A Childhood in the Countryside
passages.text:
My cousin Lan **grew up in the countryside**, in a small village far from any big city. She often tells me that her childhood was the happiest time of her life. Her house stood **on the banks of the river**, and every morning she woke to the sound of running water. Behind the house there were **woods** where she and her friends played hide-and-seek and picked wild **blackberries** in summer.

What she remembers most is how clearly she could see **the seasons** change. In spring the fields turned bright green, in autumn the leaves became red and gold, and in winter mist covered the water. The **scenery** was so beautiful that tourists sometimes stopped to take photographs, and the **natural beauty** of the valley is still famous today. Lan says that the **open spaces** and being **surrounded by nature** taught her to feel free and calm. Now she lives in a crowded city, and she misses the quiet. "I did not know how lucky I was," she says, "until I had to live without it." Every holiday she returns to her old village to walk beside the river again.

passages.title: A Health Campaign at Work
passages.text:
The health department of a large city wanted to **develop an effective strategy** to inform people about **hepatitis**, a serious liver disease that many people do not recognise. The team knew that ordinary posters would not be enough, so they decided to study how **consumers** get their health information. The research showed that most people trust short videos from doctors more than long leaflets.

Not everyone agreed on the best plan. During one meeting, a heated **argument** broke out between the designers, who wanted bright colours, and the doctors, who wanted detailed facts. The manager reminded everyone that they shared the same goal. After a difficult week, the team managed to **get through** the disagreement and agreed on a compromise: simple pictures with one clear message.

On the day of the launch, the team waited nervously for the first results. The campaign was a success, and thousands of people booked a free health check.

passages.title: A Busy Day at the Shopping Centre
passages.text:
The new shopping centre in Da Nang has five floors, and on weekends it is full of families. Mr Tuan, a security guard, watches how people move between the floors. Many shoppers **take the escalator** because it is fast and easy, especially when they are carrying shopping bags. Parents with small children, and people in wheelchairs, usually **take the elevator**, which is larger and safer. A few fitness lovers **take the stairs**, and Mr Tuan often sees them walking up all five floors without stopping.

Last Saturday, a young woman rushed past him with a worried look. "I think I **have got** coffee **on** my new white dress," she said. Mr Tuan pointed to the nearest toilet and gave her a handful of paper towels. Ten minutes later she came back smiling, with only a small mark that was almost invisible. "Thank you," she said. "Now I can enjoy my afternoon."
